summary: Discovery focused on cost/unit economics for hosted vs dedicated vs private. Lynx Capital runs production Q&A and summarization pipelines ~70k tokens/day with spiky batch loads; primary concerns are per-token unit cost, latency SLOs for trader-facing UX, and security/compliance. Redwood AE/SE covered batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization tradeoffs, and committed capacity pricing. Agreed next steps: pricing deck, security docs, benchmark run on Dedicated, and finance demo.
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-04 16:05 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Amir (Lynx Head ML), Rachel (CTO), Julian (Finance), Mae (Data Eng)

00:00 Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're running a quick agenda — cost/unit economics, current infra, and next steps.
00:12 Amir: yeah thanks, uh quick background — we're a quant research team, production ask is chat/summarization for traders. about 70k tokens a day avg, but bursts to 400k in market opens, so latency matters.
00:28 Sofia: great, and do you have a preference today — hosted API, dedicated pools, or private on prem?
00:35 Amir: open to options. right now we're on a mix — some upstream tasks with OpenAI and self-hosted smaller models. we're mostly worried about per-token costs and hitting SLAs, also procurement wants predictability.
00:48 Rachel: to add — anything that needs data residency or full on-prem will be tough; VPC/private control plane is fine. security is a hard requirement — SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs.
00:59 Ethan: understood. high level — hosted is fastest to launch and lowest up-front; dedicated gives you reserved capacity and predictable throughput; private is for full control/audit. For unit economics, the levers you can pull are batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization and model selection.
01:20 Sofia: for example, with a typical 8k context LLM, batching aggressively can cut per-token GPU compute by up to 2-3x at cost of a bit of latency tail. prefix / KV cache is huge for repeated prompts — if the first 40% of tokens are repeated, cost can go down substantially.
01:40 Julian: can you quantify — like per-token numbers? our finance folks want to see math.
01:46 Ethan: rough public numbers — hosted per-token list price for a high quality 7B-ish open model is around $0.0006 per token for generation, embeddings different. With batching and caching we often show effective per-token down to $0.0002-$0.0003 depending on hit rate and burst patterns. Dedicated reserved capacity can push unit to $0.00015-$0.00025 because of amortized GPU cost.
02:12 Amir: those ranges sound promising. how do you handle spikes — we can't have traders wait 1-2s more in opens.
02:20 Sofia: smart routing helps — hot path requests go to low-latency Dedicated nodes; cold/background work can go to cheaper pooled capacity. Also we support burst capacity on Dedicated to handle opens. In hosted, we have autoscaling but latency SLOs are softer unless you buy higher tier.
02:41 Rachel: what's the SLA on Dedicated?
02:44 Ethan: SLA-backed uptime and latency targets — we typically back 99.9% up for Dedicated with latency objectives in the contract. Exact numbers depend on reserved commit and region.
02:56 Mae: what's KV cache hit calc — do you need to change prompts to get better hits?
03:01 Sofia: KV/prefix caching works best when you have repeated prefixes or system messages. For chat, if you have standard system prompts and repeated context chunks, cache hit rate goes up. We also support chunk-level embedding-based cache for doc retrieval use cases.
03:17 Amir: ok, our QAs have a lot of repeated legalese and standard headers — sounds useful. what about quantization — will that affect output quality for our domain?
03:25 Sofia: short answer yes but tradeoff depends on model and evals. 8-bit quant reduces memory and can improve throughput; 4-bit or mixed precision saves more but we run evals on your prompt set to measure regressions. Redwood Optimize gives suggestions on model/quant profile per workload.
03:44 Julian: procurement question — committed capacity pricing, how long are terms and how does overage work?
03:49 Ethan: typical reserved terms are 1/12/36 month. you commit to a throughput/capacity level and we give discounted unit rates; overages are billed at a higher rate, with automatic burst options if you enable them. We'll model a few bands in the pricing deck.
04:05 Rachel: any compliance red flags — KMS and audit logs for Private?
04:10 Ethan: Private includes customer-managed KMS/HSM and detailed audit logs. We also have an enterprise pack with longer log retention and dedicated compliance support. We'll share the SOC2/ISO docs.
04:22 Amir: can you run numbers for our pattern — 70k daily tokens, 400k spike windows twice per day, 99th perc latency target ~350ms for short responses?
04:33 Sofia: yep, if you can share representative prompt set and token distribution we can run a benchmark. For example, on Dedicated with batching tuned to your spike profile and a 60% KV hit, you could see effective cost drop 40-60% vs naive hosted run.
04:51 Julian: that math sells. but what's the engineering lift to integrate — SDKs, VPC peering, SSO?
05:00 Ethan: SDKs are simple, REST/SDKs; VPC peering or Private control plane takes a bit more infra but we have a hands-on onboarding. SSO via SAML/SCIM and RBAC available.
05:12 Amir: any customers in finance you can point to?
05:17 Ethan: we have several, can't name all on this call but we'll add a short case study in the pack.
05:22 Mae: ok, let's talk concrete numbers — can you show a sample calculation?
05:26 Sofia: sure — rough sample: baseline hosted list is $0.0006/token gen. If your average request is 200 tokens, naive cost per request is $0.12. With batching to 4x effective throughput, that's $0.03 per request. With a 50% KV hit on the first 80 tokens, that's another 20-30% saving, so you get to ~ $0.02 per request. Dedicated with commit might bring it to $0.015.
05:56 Julian: so monthly cost ballpark for 70k/day with those savings?
06:01 Ethan: 70k * avg 200 = 14M tokens/month. At $0.0002 effective token that's $2,800/month; naive hosted at $0.0006 is $8,400/month. But spikes add network and burst costs — which we model in the deck.
06:20 Rachel: are there fixed fees for Dedicated?
06:23 Ethan: there is a platform fee and reserved GPU commit. We'll show both a capex-like committed price and an op-ex hosted comparison.
06:30 Amir: any limits on model choice — do you lock us into certain open models?
06:33 Sofia: No, you can pick from our catalog; for Dedicated we validate model performance, and we can host customer models in Private as well. Some quantization/compilation optimizations depend on model architecture.
06:44 Julian: how do you handle monitoring and cost visibility?
06:48 Ethan: Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-route breakdowns, and estimated unit cost. You can set alerts on burn rate and export traces for audit.
06:56 Mae: QA — how noisy is the transcript of our own prompts in the evals, any leakage?
06:59 Ethan: we treat all customer data as private, logs/audits under your retention policy; Private gives full on-prem control.
07:07 Amir: ok good. can you share an example of batching config and expected latency tradeoffs?
07:12 Sofia: example: dynamic batching window of 8-20ms for low-latency path yields 5-8% latency added but 2x throughput. For dark traffic we use larger windows. We can tune per-route.
07:24 Rachel: finance will want a 3-line cost comparison table — hosted, dedicated, private — with assumptions.
07:29 Ethan: we'll include that; we usually show list price, assumed batching hit, KV hit, and effective unit.
07:35 Julian: procurement timeline? if numbers look good we can do a POC in 2-3 weeks, procurement 4-6 weeks.
07:42 Ethan: sounds reasonable. we'll plan the bench and POC.
07:46 Amir: one more — if we start hosted then move to dedicated, how seamless is migration?
07:51 Sofia: pretty seamless — same API and rollout policies. You can pin model versions. We support canary and gradual traffic shift to Dedicated.
07:59 Mae: is there estimate of engineering time to get to production?
08:03 Ethan: for a standard integration with SDKs and SSO, 2-4 weeks with Redwood support. Private deployments add infra time — estimate varies.
08:12 Julian: fine. next steps?
08:15 Ethan: action items: Amir to send prompt set; Sofia to prepare benchmark plan and run Dedicated vs Hosted; Ethan to send pricing bands and security docs; schedule a 30-min benchmark session week of 3/9; finance demo for Julian and team.
08:33 Rachel: thanks all, that was useful.
08:36 Ethan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with materials.

Transcript notes: occasional ASR errors, speaker overlap early in call, some proper nouns slightly garbled (we'll provide raw recording on request).
